messages:
pagerbot: Pager — P1: High tail latency and 5xx spike on /v1/generate (hosted-api-prod). Alert rule: latency_99p > 1200ms for 5m.

maya: I'm on it. seeing customer error rate up ~18% across multiple tenants. tagging @jon @sanjay. linking grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abcd/hosted-api?panel=latency

jon: joining. first callout: check GPU pool utilization, HPA status, and queue depth on the runtime. can someone run kube checks for runtime pods and hpa?

sanjay: running checks now. posting snippets.

sanjay: ```
# kubectl get pods -n inference -l app=runtime -o wide
NAME                                      READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE   NODE
runtime-0                                 1/1     Running   0          3d   gpu-node-12
runtime-1                                 0/1     Running   1          2h   gpu-node-13
runtime-2                                 0/1     Running   0          6m   gpu-node-14
warmup-helper-0                            0/1     Init:0/1  0          5m   gpu-node-14
```

sanjay: HPA check: ```
# kubectl get hpa -n inference runtime-hpa -o yaml
metrics:
  - type: Resource
    resource:
      name: cpu
      target:
        type: Utilization
        averageUtilization: 60
behavior: {}
status:
  currentCPUUtilizationPercentage: 22
  currentReplicas: 3
  desiredReplicas: 3
```

jon: that HPA config is the smoking gun. we're autoscaling on CPU but work is GPU-bound and queue depth is what matters. CPU never rose so HPA didn't add replicas.

maya: confirmed queue depth spike on queue-metrics: ```
name: request-queue
10:12:00 -> depth: 12
10:13:00 -> depth: 48
10:14:00 -> depth: 94
10:15:00 -> depth: 160
serving_latency_p50: 210ms
serving_latency_p95: 1.1s
serving_latency_p99: 2.4s
```

maya: also warmup helper pods started but stuck initializing model weights — warmup timeouts at ~90-120s. logs show repeated "waiting for GPU memory".

henry: customer-impact check: Billing tier A customers saw 20-30% failed requests, a handful hit SLOs. pinging success to prep notifications.

deploy-bot: Deployment check: No recent runtime image pushes in last 6h. Canary rollout: none.

elaine: I'm going to temporarily scale the dedicated GPU pool manually and adjust routing. doing infractl command now.

elaine: `infractl scale --pool gpu-hosted-primary --count 10` -> accepted. provisioning nodes; ETA ~3m.

sanjay: while nodes are provisioning, we need an in-band mitigation that doesn't rely on new nodes: reduce token limits and disable large-batch merging to reduce per-request GPU time. maya can you change routing limits?

maya: setting model fallback for high-latency requests to medium-latency variant and capping max_tokens=512 for hosted-api-prod route. applying now.

maya: `route update --route hosted-api-prod --model redwood-medium --max-tokens 512 --batching off` -> applied.

jon: good. also adding temporary HPA override to scale to 6 replicas while we fix the metric. `kubectl scale deployment/runtime --replicas=6 -n inference`

sanjay: scaled to 6. verifying pod readiness... some warmup helpers still stuck but more runtime pods in Ready state now.

sanjay: warmup logs snippet: ```
E0302 10:16:24 warmup.go:72] warmup: model_init: allocator waiting for GPU memory free, retrying (attempt 3)
W0302 10:16:40 warmup.go:80] warmup: heavy serialization time: 24.2s
```

jon: hypothesis list (in-thread):
- primary root: autoscaling metric mismatch — using CPU instead of queue/gpu-util metrics. HPA never scaled up automatically.
- contributing: warmup subsystem blocked on GPU memory availability / serialization causing long init times so new pods weren't Ready quickly.
- contributing: sudden request pattern included many long-context requests increasing token compute per request.
- mitigation worked: manual scale + routing to smaller model + token cap reduced tail.

maya: confirm metrics look better now: tail latency dropping and queue depth trending down. grafana snapshot: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abcd/hosted-api?panel=queue-depth

henry: customer impact summary for incident report: 3 enterprise customers affected (partial degradation), several PLAY accounts saw elevated error rates but auto-retries mitigated visible errors. adding numbers to incident doc.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0421 (severity P1). Pager rotation: @maya -> primary, @jon -> secondary.

elaine: taking post-incident tasks: I'll open an ops ticket to change HPA to use custom queue-length metric and/or GPU util. Also adding a warmup-instrumentation task to measure model init time.

elaine: ticket created: OPS-1129 - "HPA metric migration + warmup instrumentation". assigning to eng-platform + eng-runtime. ETA for PR: 2 days.

jon: for RCA we need timeline, logs (serving, warmup, autoscaler events), and config diffs. I'll collect `kubectl describe hpa` events and autoscaler-controller logs and drop into the incident doc.

sanjay: sharing a short timeline we can use in the doc:
- 10:11:22 pagerbot alert — increased 99p latency
- 10:12:05 queue depth rising above 50
- 10:13:00 warmup helper pods start for new replicas
- 10:14:30 HPA checked — CPU at 22%, no scale triggered
- 10:15:10 manual scale to 6 replicas by @jon
- 10:16:40 routing changed to redwood-medium + max_tokens cap by @maya
- 10:18:05 tail latency falling, queue depth decreasing

maya: handing over to @elaine for post-mortem ownership. I'll remain available for notes. please include customer notifications timeline in the postmortem.

elaine: oncall handover ack. I'll coordinate the RCA write-up, add timeline, paste logs, and recommend HPA metric changes and a warmup SLO. assigning follow-ups to eng-runtime (sanjay, jon) and eng-platform (elaine).

henry: leaving a short follow-up note for support: customers notified at 10:22 UTC, follow-up emails drafted.

maya: thanks all — good coordination. closing incident channel when RCA doc is up.

deploy-bot: Note: manual scale events and route updates were recorded in deploy logs: https://deploy.redwood.internal/logs/2198765432

incident-bot: Next: create RCA doc in Confluence and link back to INC-2026-0421. Handing off to @elaine for document creation.

elaine: (last message) creating RCA doc now: https://confluence.redwood.internal/display/INC/INC-2026-0421-RCA. will include actions: HPA->queue-metric, warmup timeouts -> increase parallelism for init, short-term: keep route fallback and token cap for 24h.
